summary: Graciosa Airport (GRW/LPGR) is a small regional airport serving Santa Cruz da Graciosa on Graciosa Island, one of the nine islands of the Azores archipelago in the North Atlantic. It provides essential air connectivity between the island and other Azorean destinations, particularly São Miguel and Terceira. The airport plays a vital role in supporting tourism and local travel on this UNESCO Biosphere Reserve island, known for its volcanic landscapes and historic windmills.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Graciosa Airport?
A: SATA Air Açores is the primary carrier operating inter-island flights connecting Graciosa to other Azorean islands, mainly via Ponta Delgada and Lajes on Terceira.

Q: How long is the runway at Graciosa Airport?
A: The airport has a single runway approximately 1,250 meters long, suitable for the small regional turboprop aircraft typically used for inter-island service.

Q: Is there public transport available from the airport?
A: The airport is located very close to Santa Cruz da Graciosa, and taxis or pre-arranged transfers are the most common options, as public bus service is limited on the small island.

Q: When is the best time to visit Graciosa?
A: The island enjoys a mild subtropical climate year-round, but the summer months from June to September offer the warmest temperatures and calmest seas for outdoor activities and hiking.
transport_tips: The airport is just a few kilometers from Santa Cruz da Graciosa town center, making taxi rides quick and inexpensive. Renting a car on Graciosa is highly recommended to explore the island's volcanic caves, thermal pools at Termas do Carapacho, and scenic viewpoints at your own pace. Ferry services from Praia da Vitória on Terceira also provide an alternative way to reach the island, complementing air travel options.
local_tip: Visit the Furna do Enxofre, a stunning volcanic cave with an underground lake and sulfur vents, accessible via a spiral staircase carved into the crater wall, near Santa Cruz da Graciosa.
